intro: Think of と as a partner marker: it puts something next to something else as an equal. Two nouns side by side make a closed list (A と B). A person beside you is someone you act with (友達と). A relationship needs two sides, and と marks the other side (田中さんと結婚する). Quoting works the same way: と draws the line where the quoted words end and your own sentence picks up again.

skills.rule: Join nouns with と when you are naming all of them; the particle for the whole group goes after the last noun.
skills.explain:
と means "and" between nouns, and the list is complete: パンと牛乳を買った says you bought bread and milk, and nothing else worth mentioning. Put と between the items and the case particle (が, を, に ...) once, after the last item: 田中さんと山田さんが来ました.

と joins nouns only. It cannot link adjectives, verbs or whole clauses the way English "and" does. Adjectives and actions are joined with the て-form (安くておいしい, 起きて顔を洗う), and sentences with そして.

If the items are only examples from a longer list ("things like bread and milk"), use や instead, often closed with など. Writing と after the last item too (AとBと) is possible in careful lists but never required.

examples.jp: 犬[いぬ]{と}猫[ねこ]がいます。
examples.en: There is a dog and a cat.

examples.jp: パン{と}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]を買[か]いました。
examples.en: I bought bread and milk.

examples.jp: 月曜日[げつようび]{と}木曜日[もくようび]は休[やす]みです。
examples.en: Monday and Thursday are my days off.

examples.jp: 兄[あに]{と}私[わたし]は同[おな]じ学校[がっこう]に通[かよ]っていました。
examples.en: My older brother and I went to the same school.

examples.jp: 山田[やまだ]さんは日本語[にほんご]{と}英語[えいご]{と}中国語[ちゅうごくご]を話[はな]します。
examples.en: Ms. Yamada speaks Japanese, English and Chinese.

contrast.note: や gives examples from an open list: パンや牛乳を買った = I bought bread, milk and so on. と says the list is complete.
も means "also" and follows a single noun: 犬も猫もいる = there are both dogs and cats (emphasis on each). It does not sit between two nouns as a plain "and".
か between nouns means "or": コーヒーか紅茶 = coffee or tea, one of the two.

mistakes.bad: この店[みせ]は安[やす]い{と}おいしいです。
mistakes.good: この店[みせ]は安[やす]く{て}おいしいです。
mistakes.note: と cannot join adjectives; use the て-form (安くて) for "cheap and tasty".

mistakes.bad: 週末[しゅうまつ]は掃除[そうじ]をする{と}洗濯[せんたく]をします。
mistakes.good: 週末[しゅうまつ]は掃除[そうじ]{と}洗濯[せんたく]をします。
mistakes.note: After a verb, と means "whenever" or "if", not "and". Join the activities as nouns (掃除と洗濯), or join the verbs with たり or the て-form.

skills.tip: Two or more nouns, and that is the whole list? と. Just examples? や. Anything that is not a noun? Not と.

skills.rule: The person you do something together with takes と; add 一緒に to stress the togetherness.
skills.explain:
と marks a companion: someone who takes part in the action alongside you. 友達と映画を見た = I watched a film with a friend. 一緒に (together) is often added but adds no new grammar: 母と一緒に買い物に行く.

English "with" covers several Japanese particles, and this is where learners slip. A companion takes と. A tool or means takes で: 箸で食べる (eat with chopsticks), never 箸と. Doing something alone is 一人で, not 一人と.

With verbs of communication, と and に differ in direction. 友達と話す is a conversation between two people; 友達に話す is telling something to a friend, one way. Ask whether the other person is a partner (と) or a receiver (に).

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]{と}映画[えいが]を見[み]ました。
examples.en: I watched a film with a friend.

examples.jp: 母[はは]{と}買[か]い物[もの]に行[い]きます。
examples.en: I'm going shopping with my mother.

examples.jp: 誰[だれ]{と}来[き]ましたか。
examples.en: Who did you come with?

examples.jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]は家族[かぞく]{と}一緒[いっしょ]に過[す]ごしました。
examples.en: I spent the weekend with my family.

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]、田中[たなか]さん{と}電話[でんわ]で話[はな]しました。
examples.en: Yesterday I talked with Mr. Tanaka on the phone.

contrast.note: で marks the tool or means: ペンで書く = write with a pen. と is only for partners who take part in the action.
に marks a one-way receiver: 先生に話す = tell the teacher. 先生と話す = have a talk with the teacher.

mistakes.note: Chopsticks are a tool, so they take で. 箸と would mean the chopsticks are eating with you.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]{に}一緒[いっしょ]に遊[あそ]びました。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]{と}一緒[いっしょ]に遊[あそ]びました。
mistakes.note: The person you do something 一緒に with is marked by と: the friend is a partner, not a receiver.

skills.tip: Is the person doing it alongside you? と. Is it a thing in your hand? で.

skills.rule: End quoted words or the content of a thought with と, before 言う, 思う, 聞く, 書く and similar verbs.
skills.explain:
と closes a quotation. Direct speech goes in brackets: 「ありがとう」と言った. Reported speech and thoughts use the plain form before と: 明日来ると言った, 雨が降ると思う. The verb after と says what was done with the words: 言う (say), 思う (think), 聞く (hear, ask), 書く (write), 答える (answer).

Before と, nouns and na-adjectives need だ in the present: 学生だと言った, 静かだと思う. Dropping the だ is a common mistake. Polite forms do not go before と思う: say 行くと思います, not 行きますと思います. 行こうと思う (volitional + と思う) means "I'm thinking of going".

を marks a noun as object (名前を言う = say the name), but a quoted sentence always takes と. 〜という links a name or description to a noun: 「さくら」という店 = a shop called Sakura. In casual speech って replaces と.

examples.jp: 「ありがとう」{と}言[い]いました。
examples.en: I said "Thank you."

examples.jp: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]が降[ふ]る{と}思[おも]います。
examples.en: I think it will rain tomorrow.

examples.jp: この映画[えいが]は面白[おもしろ]くない{と}思[おも]う。
examples.en: I don't think this film is interesting.

examples.jp: 先生[せんせい]は来週[らいしゅう]テストがある{と}言[い]いました。
examples.en: The teacher said there will be a test next week.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]に「さくら」{と}いう店[みせ]があります。
examples.en: In front of the station there is a shop called Sakura.

contrast.note: を takes a noun: 名前を言う = say (your) name. A quoted sentence or thought takes と: 「田中です」と言う.
って is the casual spoken form of the quoting と: 行くって言ってた. Use と in writing and polite speech.

mistakes.bad: この部屋[へや]は静[しず]か{と}思[おも]います。
mistakes.good: この部屋[へや]は静[しず]かだ{と}思[おも]います。
mistakes.note: A na-adjective or noun needs だ before the quoting と.

mistakes.bad: 明日[あした]行[い]きます{を}思[おも]います。
mistakes.good: 明日[あした]行[い]こう{と}思[おも]います。
mistakes.note: Thought content takes と, never を, and the verb before と思う is plain, not polite; the volitional 行こう gives "I'm thinking of going".

skills.tip: Could you put quotation marks around it? Then it ends in と.

skills.rule: Verbs and adjectives that need two sides (結婚する, けんかする, 別れる, 同じ, 違う) mark the other side with と.
skills.explain:
Some actions and relations cannot exist with one party: you marry someone, fight with someone, break up with someone, are the same as or different from something. Japanese marks the other party with と: 姉は高校の同級生と結婚した, 弟とけんかした, 私の意見は田中さんと同じだ, 今は昔と違う.

This is not the companion と. In 友達とけんかした, the friend is not on your side; they are the other side of the fight. The grammar is the same particle because both people are needed.

English speakers reach for を because "marry" takes a direct object in English: 彼を結婚する is wrong. A few verbs also accept に, notably 似ている (母に似ている and 母と似ている are both fine) and 比べる (去年と比べて / 去年に比べて). 結婚する, けんかする, 同じ and 違う take only と.
patterns: [A] は [B] と 結婚する／けんかする／別れる
[A] は [B] と 同じだ／違う

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]{と}けんかしました。
examples.en: I had a fight with my younger brother.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]の意見[いけん]は田中[たなか]さん{と}同[おな]じです。
examples.en: My opinion is the same as Mr. Tanaka's.

examples.jp: 姉[あね]は去年[きょねん]、高校[こうこう]の同級生[どうきゅうせい]{と}結婚[けっこん]しました。
examples.en: Last year my older sister married a classmate from high school.

examples.jp: この町[まち]は十年前[じゅうねんまえ]{と}全然[ぜんぜん]違[ちが]います。
examples.en: This town is completely different from ten years ago.

examples.jp: 去年[きょねん]{と}比[くら]べて、今年[ことし]は雪[ゆき]が多[おお]いです。
examples.en: Compared with last year, there is a lot of snow this year.

contrast.note: English "marry X" has no preposition, but in Japanese the spouse is a partner, not an object: 山田さんと結婚する, never 山田さんを.
に marks a one-way target. A few words such as 似ている and 比べる accept に as well as と, but 結婚する, けんかする, 同じ and 違う take と.

mistakes.bad: 田中[たなか]さんは山田[やまだ]さん{を}結婚[けっこん]しました。
mistakes.good: 田中[たなか]さんは山田[やまだ]さん{と}結婚[けっこん]しました。
mistakes.note: 結婚する takes the spouse with と, not を.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]のかばんはあなたの{に}同[おな]じです。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]のかばんはあなたの{と}同[おな]じです。
mistakes.note: 同じ marks what it is compared with by と.

skills.tip: Does it take two to do it, or to compare? The second one takes と.
